Lich Survivors · round 46 · the burned mask: what real fire does

2026-10-04. References only: nothing is built yet. Real photographs of real fire damage (no burned masks exist among sources; these are the nearest things).

You said the mask looks artificial, as if the damage was not real. The current one is a drawn idea of burning: an even black, soot tongues, blisters. Real burning follows the object: soot climbs from where the flame was, thin edges go first, wood breaks into cracked char, paint lifts. Before rebuilding it, which material is it, and which kind of damage? Pick a direction (A, B, C or D), and point at any photos you want it to look like. The claw gashes and the pierced left eye from your drawing stay unless you say otherwise. They match the lore now: the giant creature's claw and the flying insect that went through the prince's head.

Now

A · SOOTED WHITE

The mask stays a white mask; the fire was below it and to one side. Soot climbs from where the flame was and thins out upward in streaks, ending in a ragged tide line over clean white. Thin edges and raised features catch more than the hollows. Nothing burns through. It would read as his mask, the lich's white one, with something terrible having happened near it.

B · CHARRED

The mask was wood and it burned: carbon, black and dull, broken into the cracked blocks of charred wood (the crocodile skin), smaller and glossier where it burned hottest. The thin parts go first: the rim, the edges of the eye slits and the gashes eaten back ragged. Carved relief melts into lumps. The current mask is closest to this, but has no real char pattern and no eaten edges.

C · PAINT OVER CHAR

A white painted (gesso or lacquer) mask over wood: the white layer blisters, browns, lifts and flakes off, and under it the wood is charred black. Patches of white survive where the heat was least, with scorched brown frills round them. Between A and B: it keeps some white, and the burned parts are real char.

D · MELTED

The mask was something that melts (resin, glaze, plastic): it sags and drips, bubbles and pits. Probably not this mask, but here so the choice is seen.
